zh: 返程必须严格晚于出发（j>i），所以不能简单地把两个数组各自的最小值相加。
固定出发日 i 时，最优的返程票价就是 returning[i+1..n−1] 中的最小值；从右往左扫描，可以在 O(1) 内维护这个后缀最小值。
先把后缀最小值设为最后一天的返程票价、答案设为倒数第二天的去程票价加上它；然后 i 从 n−2 递减到 0，先用 returning[i+1] 更新后缀最小值，再用 departing[i] 加后缀最小值更新答案。票价可以为负，求和用 64 位整数。
en: The return must be strictly later than the departure (j > i), so simply adding the minimums of the two arrays is wrong.
For a fixed departure day i, the best return fare is the minimum of returning[i+1..n-1]; scanning from right to left maintains that suffix minimum in O(1) per step.

Start with the suffix minimum equal to the last day's return fare and the answer equal to the second-to-last day's departure fare plus it; then for i from n-2 down to 0, first update the suffix minimum with returning[i+1], then update the answer with departing[i] plus the suffix minimum. Fares can be negative; use 64-bit sums.

explanationEn:
## Approach

When iterating over the departure day i, the return must come later, so only returning[i+1..n-1] is considered. Scan from right to left while maintaining the minimum fare in that range, add it to departing[i], and update the answer.

## Proof of correctness

For any fixed departure day i, the valid return days are exactly j>i; the suffix minimum is exactly the minimum among these valid return fares, so adding it to departing[i] gives the optimal valid cost for that i. Taking the minimum after iterating over every i covers all valid departure days, so the global optimum is obtained.

## Complexity

Time O(n), extra space O(1) (excluding the input arrays).

## Source and site conventions

The fixed OAMaster snapshot (https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/meta#24-get-minimum-round-trip-cost, content fingerprint a593c760ead9bffff0c1e7bdc69f17028ece67e9f8641d955b24c057c08bd53c) gives the array definitions and the original example but omits the return-day restriction; its example solutions in three languages take the minimum of each array separately and ignore the order of the days. The 1Point3Acres report of the same problem explicitly requires j>i: https://www.1point3acres.com/interview/problems/meta-solve-transportation-problem. Under this strict condition the original example is still 2 (outbound fare 1 on day 0, return fare 1 on day 3). The snapshot gives no constraints; n, the fare range, and the stdin/stdout protocol on this site are all supplementary conventions.
